title: Python Tutorial (Official Documentation)
description: The language's own introduction, walking through syntax, data structures, functions and modules. Dry but authoritative and complete. Best for learners who prefer reading reference material to watching videos.

title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python
description: A free online book that teaches Python through small practical automation tasks rather than abstract exercises. Covers files, spreadsheets and simple scripting. Strong choice for total beginners who need motivation from visible results.

title: Kaggle Learn: Python
description: A short hands-on course covering the Python needed for data work specifically, skipping general-purpose topics. Runs entirely in the browser with exercises checked automatically.
notes: LINK: high confidence. Requires free Kaggle account.

title: Kaggle Learn: Pandas
description: Covers indexing, selecting, grouping and combining DataFrames with immediate exercises on real datasets. Assumes basic Python already.

title: Kaggle Learn: Data Cleaning
description: Focused module on missing values, scaling, inconsistent text entry and character encoding problems. Short and practical.

title: Kaggle Learn: Data Visualization
description: Teaches chart selection and plotting with Seaborn, emphasising which chart answers which question. Light on theory, heavy on doing.

title: Kaggle Learn: Intro to SQL
description: Introduces SELECT, WHERE, GROUP BY and simple aggregation against real query engines. Good first exposure for someone who has never queried a database.

title: SQLBolt: Learn SQL with Interactive Exercises
description: Browser-based lessons that build from single-table selects up to joins, each with an exercise you must pass before continuing. No signup and no setup at all.
notes: LINK: high confidence. Best zero-friction SQL starting point.

title: Mode SQL Tutorial
description: A three-part tutorial moving from basic to intermediate to advanced SQL, framed around analyst work rather than database administration. Includes a live editor against real datasets.

title: Kaggle Learn: Advanced SQL
description: Covers joins, unions, analytic window functions and nested data. The natural follow-on once basic querying is comfortable.

title: HackerRank SQL Practice
description: A graded problem set spanning basic selects through advanced joins and aggregation. Useful for testing whether SQL knowledge actually holds up under a timed question.

title: DataLemur SQL Interview Questions
description: Real SQL interview questions from data companies, with difficulty labels and solutions. Aimed squarely at people preparing for analyst interviews.
notes: LINK: verify — free tier scope may have changed.

title: PostgreSQL Tutorial
description: A structured reference covering PostgreSQL from querying through schema design, indexes and constraints. Includes a sample database to practise against.

title: NumPy: The Absolute Basics for Beginners
description: The official onboarding guide to arrays, shapes, indexing and broadcasting. Concise and correct; read it once before touching pandas seriously.

title: Pandas Getting Started Tutorials
description: Ten short official tutorials each answering one practical question about loading, selecting, plotting and reshaping data. Good for filling specific gaps rather than reading end to end.

title: freeCodeCamp: Data Analysis with Python
description: A full certification covering NumPy, pandas and data cleaning, ending in five required projects. The projects are the value here; the video lectures are optional.

title: freeCodeCamp: Scientific Computing with Python
description: Python fundamentals taught through computation-oriented problems, finishing with five build-it-yourself projects. Slower than Kaggle Learn but far more practice per concept.

title: Matplotlib Tutorials
description: Official tutorials from basic plotting through the object-oriented interface and styling. Necessary once default charts stop being enough.

title: Seaborn Official Tutorial
description: Walks through the library's plot families and the grammar behind them. Assumes pandas familiarity and some Matplotlib exposure.

title: Khan Academy: Statistics and Probability
description: A complete free statistics curriculum from summary measures through probability, inference and significance testing, with practice exercises throughout. The most reliable no-cost path for someone with no statistics background.
notes: LINK: high confidence. Long — usually assigned in parts.

title: Seeing Theory
description: Interactive visual explanations of probability and inference concepts. Excellent as a companion when a formula-first treatment isn't landing, weak as a sole source.

title: StatQuest with Josh Starmer
description: A large catalogue of short videos explaining statistical and machine learning concepts from first principles. Best used to unblock one specific concept rather than watched in sequence.
notes: LINK: high confidence. Channel, not a structured course.

title: 3Blue1Brown: Essence of Linear Algebra
description: A visual series building geometric intuition for vectors, matrices, determinants and eigenvectors. Builds understanding rather than computational fluency, so pair it with exercises.

title: Khan Academy: Linear Algebra
description: Systematic coverage of vectors, matrix operations, transformations and eigenvalues with practice problems. The computational counterpart to a visual series.

title: Kaggle Learn: Intro to Machine Learning
description: Builds a first decision tree and random forest model end to end, introducing train/test splits and validation error. Deliberately shallow on theory.

title: Kaggle Learn: Intermediate Machine Learning
description: Handles missing values, categorical variables, pipelines, cross-validation and gradient boosting. The step that turns a toy model into a defensible one.

title: Kaggle Learn: Feature Engineering
description: Covers mutual information, feature creation, clustering and target encoding as inputs to a model. Practical and short.

title: Kaggle Learn: Time Series
description: Covers trend, seasonality and serial dependence, then builds forecasting models that combine them. Works on real time-indexed datasets rather than synthetic series. Applied throughout, with almost no theoretical derivation, so pair it with a statistics source if forecasting becomes a main focus.

title: Kaggle Learn: Intro to Deep Learning
description: Builds neural networks with Keras, covering layers, activations, overfitting and training curves. A gentle entry point that skips most of the mathematics.

title: scikit-learn: Getting Started
description: A compressed tour of estimators, transformers, pipelines and model selection. Short enough to read in one sitting and orients you in the library's design.

title: scikit-learn User Guide
description: The full reference covering supervised and unsupervised methods, preprocessing and evaluation with the theory behind each. A reference to consult, not a course to complete.

title: freeCodeCamp: Machine Learning with Python
description: TensorFlow-centred introduction to core ML and neural networks, with five certification projects. Project-heavy, which is what makes it worth the time.

title: Kaggle: Titanic — Machine Learning from Disaster
description: The standard first end-to-end modelling exercise: clean a small messy dataset, engineer features and submit predictions. Its value is the full loop, not the problem itself.

title: Kaggle: House Prices — Advanced Regression Techniques
description: A regression problem with enough messy features to force real preprocessing and feature engineering decisions. A good second project once a first model has been shipped.

title: Google Colab: Welcome Notebook
description: The zero-install notebook environment with free compute. Worth twenty minutes early so that no later resource is blocked on a local Python setup.

title: Jupyter Documentation
description: Official documentation on running, configuring and organising notebooks locally. Useful once browser-based notebooks stop being sufficient.

title: Microsoft Learn: Power BI Training
description: Structured modules on connecting data sources, modelling and building reports in Power BI. Free, first-party and mapped to the certification.
notes: LINK: verify — Microsoft Learn paths get reorganised.

title: Tableau Free Training Videos
description: First-party video training covering connections, calculations and dashboard construction. Best for someone whose target employer already uses Tableau.

title: Storytelling with Data — Blog
description: Detailed chart makeovers showing why a visual failed and what a better version communicates. The clearest free material on presenting analysis to a non-technical audience.

title: Exceljet: Excel Formulas and Functions
description: A searchable library of worked formula examples with explanations, covering lookups, conditionals and aggregation. Reference material rather than a course.
notes: LINK: verify path — site sections have been restructured before.

title: A/B Testing — Optimizely Optimization Glossary
description: A clear practitioner's overview of what an A/B test is, how it is run and the common ways teams misread results. Short introduction, not a statistics course.

title: StrataScratch Data Science Practice Problems
description: Interview-style SQL and Python problems drawn from real company screens, with community solutions. Free tier is limited but sufficient for practice.

title: Google Data Analytics Professional Certificate
description: An eight-course programme covering the analyst workflow from question framing through spreadsheets, SQL, R and dashboards. Auditable free; the certificate is paid. Its strength is structure and career framing for career-changers.
notes: LINK: high confidence. Very long — usually only partially assigned.

title: MIT OpenCourseWare: Introduction to Computational Thinking and Data Science
description: University-level lectures on optimisation, stochastic models and statistical reasoning in Python. Considerably more rigorous than bootcamp material and appropriate for someone who wants the theory.
notes: LINK: verify — OCW course URLs include the term and can change.

title: Full Stack Deep Learning — Course Materials
description: Covers taking models beyond a notebook: infrastructure, testing, deployment and monitoring. Aimed at people who can already train a model and now need it to run somewhere.

title: Practical Deep Learning for Coders
description: A top-down course that has learners training working models in the first lesson before unpacking the theory. Suits people who learn by building; frustrating for those who want foundations first.

title: Hugging Face NLP Course
description: Working with transformer models for text classification, tokenisation and fine-tuning, using the library the field actually uses. Assumes comfort with Python and some ML exposure.

title: Data Cleaning Project: Messy Dataset Practice
description: An open dataset catalogue to pick a genuinely messy real-world file and take it from raw to analysis-ready. Unstructured by design — the point is practising judgement without a tutorial's guardrails.
notes: LINK: high confidence. Self-directed, not a guided course.

title: Database Design Course — freeCodeCamp
description: A long-form video covering entity relationships, keys, normal forms and schema design decisions. Sound content; the length means it works better consulted in sections.
notes: LINK: verify — YouTube video ID should be confirmed.

title: Khan Academy: AP Statistics — Significance Tests
description: Focused treatment of sampling distributions, confidence intervals and significance testing at exam depth. Narrower and more rigorous than the general statistics track.

title: MDN: Learn Web Development
description: Mozilla's structured curriculum from first HTML page through CSS, JavaScript and tooling. The most reliable free reference on the web platform, written by people who document the standards.
notes: LINK: verify — MDN moved /docs/Learn to /docs/Learn_web_development; old path redirects.

title: MDN: Structuring Content with HTML
description: Semantic elements, document structure, forms, tables and media, with the reasoning behind each choice. Covers the markup decisions that later determine accessibility.
notes: LINK: verify — MDN restructured its Learn section.

title: MDN: CSS Styling Basics
description: Selectors, the cascade, the box model, typography and layout fundamentals. Explains why CSS behaves as it does rather than listing properties.

title: freeCodeCamp: Responsive Web Design Certification
description: Builds HTML and CSS from scratch through guided projects, ending with five independent builds. The project requirements are what make the knowledge stick.

title: Flexbox Froggy
description: A puzzle game teaching flexbox properties across twenty-four levels. Roughly an hour, and it removes most of the guesswork people carry about alignment for years.

title: Grid Garden
description: The same puzzle format applied to CSS Grid, covering tracks, lines and areas. Short and effective as a first exposure to two-dimensional layout.

title: CSS-Tricks: A Complete Guide to Flexbox
description: The reference diagram every developer returns to, showing each flex property and its visual effect. Reference material rather than instruction.

title: CSS-Tricks: A Complete Guide to CSS Grid
description: The companion Grid reference covering template areas, sizing functions and placement. Pairs well with a hands-on exercise.

title: javascript.info — The Modern JavaScript Tutorial
description: A deep, well-sequenced treatment of the language from basics through prototypes, promises and modules. Thorough enough to serve as a primary source and a long-term reference.

title: freeCodeCamp: JavaScript Algorithms and Data Structures
description: Language fundamentals plus algorithmic problem-solving, ending in five certification projects. The algorithm sections double as interview preparation.

title: MDN: Asynchronous JavaScript
description: Callbacks, promises, async/await and the event loop, with the failure modes each one introduces. The concept most self-taught developers half-understand.

title: MDN: Fetch API
description: Reference documentation for making HTTP requests from the browser, including headers, response handling and errors. Consult it rather than read it front to back.

title: The Odin Project: Foundations
description: A curated full-stack path covering command line, Git, HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with projects at each stage. Notable for teaching the surrounding tooling most courses skip.

title: The Odin Project: Full Stack JavaScript
description: Continues from the foundations into React, Node, Express and databases with substantial independent projects. Demanding and largely self-directed.
notes: LINK: high confidence. Very long — assign specific sections.

title: React: Learn React (Official Docs)
description: The rewritten official tutorial covering components, props, state and effects with interactive examples. Now the best single React starting point.

title: React: Thinking in React
description: A short guide to decomposing a design into a component tree and deciding where state belongs. The architectural habit that separates working React from maintainable React.

title: freeCodeCamp: Front End Development Libraries
description: Covers Bootstrap, jQuery, Sass, React and Redux with five certification projects. The React and Redux sections are the reason to take it; the jQuery material is dated.
notes: LINK: high confidence. Partly dated curriculum.

title: Next.js Learn
description: An interactive course building a working dashboard application, covering routing, data fetching, streaming and deployment. Ships something real at the end.

title: TypeScript Handbook
description: Official coverage of types, interfaces, generics and configuration. Dense; most learners take the first half and return to the rest as needed.

title: Tailwind CSS: Utility-First Fundamentals
description: Explains the utility-first approach and when it beats writing custom CSS. Short, and the philosophy section matters more than the class list.
notes: LINK: verify — Tailwind renamed this docs page between major versions.

title: Node.js: Introduction and Guides
description: Official guides on the runtime, modules, the file system and asynchronous patterns outside the browser. Reference-style but current.

title: Express: Routing Guide
description: The official explanation of route definitions, parameters and middleware chaining. Short and necessary before designing any API surface.

title: freeCodeCamp: Back End Development and APIs
description: Node, Express and MongoDB through five build-and-submit API projects. Practical, though the database portion is document-oriented rather than relational.

title: Prisma: Getting Started
description: Setting up a typed database client, modelling a schema and running migrations against a relational database. The fastest route from an Express app to a working database layer.

title: JWT: Introduction to JSON Web Tokens
description: Explains token structure, signing and the cases where tokens are and are not the right choice. Necessary background before implementing any auth flow.

title: web.dev: Learn Accessibility
description: Structured modules on semantic HTML, ARIA, focus management and testing with assistive technology. Practical and standards-aligned.

title: web.dev: Learn Performance
description: Covers Core Web Vitals, resource loading, rendering and measurement methodology. Written by the team that defines the metrics browsers report.

title: MDN: Accessibility Learning Module
description: Accessibility fundamentals framed around markup decisions and testing. Overlaps with web.dev's course; pick one rather than both.

title: React Testing Library: Introduction
description: Documentation for testing components by their visible behaviour rather than internals. The philosophy section is the important part.

title: Vitest Guide
description: Setting up and writing tests with the Vite-native test runner, including mocking and coverage. Now the common default for new frontend projects.

title: Learn Git Branching
description: An interactive visualiser where branching, merging and rebasing are practised against a live commit graph. The fastest way to stop being afraid of Git.

title: Pro Git (Book)
description: The complete free Git reference from basics through internals. Chapters two and three carry most of the day-to-day value.

title: GitHub Skills
description: Short interactive exercises run inside real repositories, covering pull requests, code review and Actions. Teaches collaboration rather than the Git CLI.

title: MDN: Command Line Crash Course
description: Terminal navigation, file operations and running build tools, aimed at developers rather than system administrators.

title: Frontend Mentor Challenges
description: Real design files to build against, with a community reviewing submissions. The free tier is enough to build a portfolio, and working from a designer's spec is a skill tutorials never teach.

title: Laws of UX
description: Short entries on the psychological principles behind interface decisions, each with examples. A fast way for a developer to reason about design instead of guessing.

title: Figma: Get Started Guide
description: Official tutorials on frames, components, auto layout and prototyping. Enough to read a designer's file and build from it, which is the common developer need.
notes: LINK: verify — Figma help-centre category IDs change.

title: Refactoring UI — Free Design Tips
description: Practical rules for developers on hierarchy, spacing, colour and typography. The paid book is optional; the free material alone lifts most developer-built interfaces noticeably.
notes: LINK: verify — free vs paid split may have changed.

title: Vercel Documentation: Deployments
description: How git-connected deploys, preview environments and environment variables work. The shortest path from a local frontend to a public URL.
notes: LINK: verify — Vercel docs paths are reorganised often.

title: Netlify Documentation: Get Started
description: Connecting a repository, configuring builds and managing environment settings. Equivalent to the Vercel path; pick one.

title: React Router: Tutorial
description: Route configuration, nested layouts, parameters and navigation. Necessary for any React app past a single screen.
notes: LINK: verify — React Router docs restructured across v6/v7.

title: Zustand Documentation
description: A minimal state management library documented in a single readable page. A pragmatic answer once prop drilling and context become painful.

title: MDN: Client-side Web APIs
description: Working with browser APIs including the DOM, fetch, storage and media. Bridges language fundamentals and real application code.

title: Build a Full-Stack App: Portfolio Project
description: A community roadmap with project ideas and skill checkpoints for full-stack work. Best used as a scoping and gap-checking tool rather than instruction.
notes: LINK: high confidence. Not a course — a roadmap plus project prompts.

title: Chrome DevTools Documentation
description: Reference for the debugging, network, performance and accessibility panels. Learning the profiler properly pays back repeatedly.
